questions.question: Chhau is a major dance tradition of India. In which of the following Indian states is the dance form NOT prevalent?
questions.questionHtml: Chhau is a major dance tradition of India. In which of the following Indian states is the dance form NOT prevalent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh

Key Points

  • Chhau is a major dance tradition in India.
  • The dance form is prevalent in the states of Odisha, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.
  • Chhau is not prevalent in Madhya Pradesh.
  • Chhau dance is known for its vibrant costumes and elaborate masks, depicting various mythological and folk themes.

Additional Information

  • The Chhau dance has been recognized by UNESCO as an intangible cultural heritage.
  • It is traditionally performed during the spring festival, particularly Chaitra Parva.
  • There are three main styles of Chhau dance named after the location where they are performed: Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).
  • The dance involves martial, folk, and tribal elements, making it a unique blend of various cultural aspects.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms has been included in the UNESCO Heritage Dances in the year 2010?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following dance forms has been included in the UNESCO Heritage Dances in the year 2010?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chau.

Key Points

  • The UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation) inscribes three Indian performing-art forms, the Mudiyettu, a ritual theatre of Kerala, the Chhau dance, a tradition from eastern India, and the Kalbelia folk songs and dances of Rajasthan in the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
  • This annual list, unlike the World Heritage list that focuses on monuments and natural sites, spotlights performing art forms of outstanding value and are vulnerable due to lack of support.

Additional Information

  • Kalbelia dance
    • It is a folk dance of the Rajasthan state of India. 
    • It is well known as 'Sapera Dance' or 'Snake Charmer Dance'.
    • It is mainly performed by a Rajasthani tribe called 'Kalbelia'.
    • It is listed under UNESCO's representative list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity from the year 2010.
  • The Mudiyettu,
    • It is the ritual dance-drama annually performed after the harvest of summer crops in Kerala, which is more than 250 years old.
    • This art form involves elaborate drawings on floors, masks made of areca nut fronds, and the playing of drums.
    • What was once well patronized, now has only three traditional families of regular performers.
  • The Chhau dance,
    • It is known for its crafted masks and mock combat movements that are prevalent in the tribal parts of Orissa, Jharkhand, and West Bengal.
  • The economic backwardness of the area, an extensive survey by the Sangeet Natak Akademi reveals, has had a negative impact on the artists of the Chhau and their art. Similarly, the Kalbeli community of snake charmers from Rajasthan are also impacted.

questions.question: Mallika Sarabhai was awarded with Padma Bhushan (2010) - for contirbution to Performing Arts. She was highly recognized for which dance forms?
questions.questionHtml: Mallika Sarabhai was awarded with Padma Bhushan (2010) - for contirbution to Performing Arts. She was highly recognized for which dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam.

Key Points

  • Mallika Sarabhai:-
    • Mallika Sarabhai is an Indian Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dancer, stage actress, director, and social activist.
    • She is the daughter of dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai and prominent space scientist Vikram Sarabhai.
    • Sarabhai began learning dance from her mother at the age of 5.
    • She emerged as a professional dancer in the 1970s and has since performed all over the world. She has excelled in both Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam.
    • Sarabhai is also active as a stage actress.
    • She has acted in several plays and films, including Peter Brook's play Mahabharata in the role of Draupadi.

Additional Information

  • Bharatanatyam:
    • Bharatanatyam is the oldest of the classical Indian dances, and is said to have originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
    • It is a highly expressive dance form that combines complex footwork with graceful arm movements.
  • Kathak:
    • Kathak is a northern Indian classical dance that is known for its storytelling elements.
    • It is often performed to the accompaniment of Hindustani classical music.
  • Kathakali:
    • Kathakali is a traditional dance form from Kerala that is known for its elaborate costumes and makeup.
    • It is typically performed by men and tells stories from Hindu mythology.
  • Kuchipudi:
    • Kuchipudi is a classical dance from Andhra Pradesh that is known for its dynamic movements and expressive gestures.
    • It is often performed to the accompaniment of Telugu classical music.
  • Manipuri:
    • Manipuri is a classical dance from the northeastern state of Manipur.
    • It is known for its graceful movements and fluid transitions.
    • It is often performed to the accompaniment of Manipuri folk music.
  • Odissi:
    • Odissi is a classical dance from the eastern Indian state of Odisha.
    • It is known for its sculpturesque poses and fluid movements.
    • It is often performed to the accompaniment of Odissi classical music.

questions.question: Mahari Dance and Gotipua Dance belongs to which of the following states?
questions.questionHtml: Mahari Dance and Gotipua Dance belongs to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Odisha.

Key Points

  • Mahari Dance and Gotipua Dance are traditional dance forms that originate from the state of Odisha.
  • Mahari Dance is one of the oldest dance forms in Odisha, traditionally performed by devadasis in the Jagannath Temple of Puri.
  • Gotipua Dance is performed by young boys dressed as female dancers and is considered a precursor to the classical Odissi dance.
  • Both dance forms are integral parts of Odisha's rich cultural heritage and contribute significantly to the state's traditional arts.

Additional Information

  • Odissi is a classical dance form that evolved from these traditional dances and is recognized as one of the eight classical dance forms of India.
  • Odisha is known for its vibrant cultural heritage, which includes a variety of dance forms, music, and art.
  • The state government and various cultural organizations actively promote and preserve these traditional dance forms through festivals, workshops, and performances.

Thang Ta is also known as the art of sword and spear and is a significant part of Manipuri culture and heritage.

questions.question: Padma Subrahmanyam is a well-known dancer of which of the following dance forms?
questions.questionHtml: Padma Subrahmanyam is a well-known dancer of which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

Key Points

  • Bharatnatyam dance origin can be traced from back to Sadir-the solo dance of temple dancer or devadasis in Tamil Nadu.
  • Bharatnatyam is also known as Dashiattam.
  • Elements of Bharatnatyam
    • Alarippu-seeking blessing of god with simple dance steps in rhythm.
    • Jatiswaram-Nritta component with devoid expression.
    • Shabdam-dramatic element with expressed words.
    • Varnam-combination of dance and emotion to express a story.
    • Padam-mastery over abhinaya of a spiritual message by the artist.
    • Jawali-Its performed at short love lyrics at a fast tempo.
    • Thillana-Its is known as concluding Stage with pure dance(Nritta).
  • Padma Subramaniam is related to Bharatnatyam dance.​

questions.question: Alarmel Valli is a __________ dancer.
questions.questionHtml: Alarmel Valli is a __________ dancer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam

Key Points

  • Alarmel Valli is an acclaimed Indian classical dancer known for her expertise in Bharatnatyam.
  • Bharatnatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Tamil Nadu.
  • It is characterized by its fixed upper torso, bent legs and knees flexed out combined with spectacular footwork, and sophisticated vocabulary of hand and facial gestures.
  • Alarmel Valli has been awarded several prestigious accolades for her contribution to the art form, including the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.

Additional Information

  • The origins of Bharatnatyam can be traced back to the Natya Shastra, an ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts.
  • It is traditionally performed by women, and has its roots in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
  • The dance form was revived in the early 20th century by pioneers like Rukmini Devi Arundale and E. Krishna Iyer.
  • In modern times, Bharatnatyam is performed by both men and women and has gained global recognition.
  • Bharatnatyam performances typically involve a solo dancer who performs a variety of items, each with a distinct mood and meaning.

questions.question: Deepa Sashindran, Raja Reddy and Radha Reddy are associated with which of the following Indian dances?
questions.questionHtml: Deepa Sashindran, Raja Reddy and Radha Reddy are associated with which of the following Indian dances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is KuchipudiKey Points

  • Deepa Sashindran is a Kuchipudi dancer, and Raja Reddy and Radha Reddy are famous Kuchipudi exponents.
  • Deepa Sashindran:
    • A Kuchipudi dancer and choreographer who has performed in India and abroad.
    • She has created original works, including solo performances, dance dramas, and features.
    • She has also taught workshops and performed in Doha, Dubai, and Abu Dhabi.
  • Raja and Radha Reddy are Indian Kuchipudi dancing couples, gurus, and choreographers.
  • They are renowned as exponents of the south Indian dance form of Kuchipudi.
  • Their names are synonymous with Kuchipudi dance and are regarded solely responsible for bringing it on the cultural map of the world.
  • For their services to the field of arts, the Government of India has conferred on them the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awards.

Additional Information

  • Kuchipudi:
    • Kuchipudi is a major classical dance form of India that originated in a village of the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
    • Kuchipudi involves different foot movements and is generally a team performance.
    • The central them of Kuchipudi is Bhagavata puran.
    • The dancers of Kuchipudi came to be known as Bhagavathalus.
  • Bharatnatyam:
    • Bharatanatyam is the oldest and major classical dance form of India that originated in Tamil Nadu.
    • It traces its origins back to the Natyashastra, ancient treaties on theatre written by the mythic priest Bharata.
  • Kathakali:
    • Kathakali is a classical Indian dance form which is a story play genre of art and is the folk dance form of Kerala.
    • It is a 'story play' genre of art, but one distinguished by the elaborately colorful make-up, costumes, and face masks that the traditionally male actor-dancers wear.

questions.question: Who among the following was a renowned dancer and the first person from Odisha to receive 'Padma Vibhushan' in 2000?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was a renowned dancer and the first person from Odisha to receive 'Padma Vibhushan' in 2000?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra

Key Points

  • Kelucharan Mohapatra was a legendary Indian classical dancer, guru, and proponent of the Odissi dance form.
  • He was the first person from Odisha to receive the prestigious Padma Vibhushan award in the year 2000.
  • Kelucharan Mohapatra played a crucial role in reviving and popularizing Odissi dance globally.
  • His contribution to Indian classical dance has been immense, earning him numerous accolades and recognition worldwide.

Additional Information

  • Kelucharan Mohapatra was born on 8th January 1926 in Raghurajpur, Odisha.
  • He started his career as a Gotipua dancer and later transitioned to Odissi, under the guidance of various gurus.
  • Kelucharan Mohapatra's work includes not only performances but also extensive teaching and choreography, ensuring the continuation and growth of the Odissi dance form.
  • He established the Srjan (Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Odissi Nrityabasa) institution, which continues to train and promote young dancers in the Odissi tradition.
  • His legacy is carried forward by his students, many of whom are celebrated Odissi dancers today.

questions.question: Gambhira, Dhali and Jatra are the famous dance forms of which state?
questions.questionHtml: Gambhira, Dhali and Jatra are the famous dance forms of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

Key Points

  • Gambhira, Dhali and Jatra are the famous dance forms of West Bengal.
  • Shakti worshippers perform Gambhira, a sacred devotional dance.
  • The dance is named after the Chandi Mandir - Gambhira's dance hall, which features a specifically built pavilion in front of the shrine for the dance.
  • During the reign of Raja Pratapaditya, the Dhali Dance was born and evolved. The Dhali dance is done by two guys using cane shields and bamboo sticks as weapons.
  • Jatra Dance is famous in West Bengal. Bibek (conscience) and Niyati (fear) are two figures who grab the audience's attention in this dance form (fate).

questions.question: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma was an Indian Classical Dancer of _________ dance form.
questions.questionHtml: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma was an Indian Classical Dancer of _________ dance form.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

Key Points

  • Kalamandalam Kallyanikutty Amma was an epoch-making Mohiniyattam danseuse from Kerala in southern India.
  • Mohiniyattam is a classical Indian dance, which by definition traces its repertoire to the foundational text Natya Shastra.
  • The Natya Shastra text is attributed to the ancient scholar Bharata Muni. 
  • Its first complete compilation is dated to between 200 BCE and 200 CE, but estimates vary between 500 BCE and 500 CE.

Additional Information

  • Sattriya or Sattriya Nritya is a major Indian classical dance.
  • Odissi also mention as Orissa in old literature is a major old Indian classical dance that originated in the Hindu temples of Odisha.
  • Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance. It is the classical dance form of Uttar Pradesh.
  • The origin of Kathak is traditionally assigned to the traveling bards in ancient northern India.

questions.question: Padmaja Reddy is a famous _________ classical dancer.
questions.questionHtml: Padmaja Reddy is a famous _________ classical dancer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi .

Key Points

  • Kuchipudi:

    • Padmaja Reddy is a renowned Kuchipudi classical dancer.
    • She is known for her expressive abhinaya (acting) and graceful movements.
    • She has dedicated her life to preserving and promoting the Kuchipudi dance form.
    • She is a very respected guru of the dance form.
    • She has performed both nationally and internationally.

Additional Information

  • Kathak:

    • Kathak is a classical dance form originating from North India, known for its intricate footwork and storytelling.
    • It is characterized by spins, complex rhythmic patterns, and expressive gestures.
    • Kathak emphasizes both technical skill and emotional expression.
    • It has a rich history influenced by both Hindu and Muslim cultures.
    • The dance form is known for its use of the ghungroo.

  • Kathakali:

    • Kathakali is a classical dance-drama from Kerala, South India, known for its elaborate makeup and costumes.
    • It is characterized by its stylized gestures, facial expressions, and vigorous movements.
    • Kathakali performances often depict stories from Hindu epics and mythology.
    • It is a very theatrical dance form.
    • The training for Kathakali is very rigorous.

  • Bharatnatyam:

    • Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, South India.
    • It is known for its precise footwork, expressive hand gestures (mudras), and facial expressions (abhinaya).
    • Bharatanatyam is traditionally a solo dance performed by women.
    • It has a strong spiritual and devotional element.
    • It is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India.

questions.question: Sitara Devi was a ________ dancer of India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is KathakKey Points

  • Kathak is a classical dance form that is usually performed solo and focuses on footwork.

questions.question: How many classical dance forms does the Sangeet Natak Akademi in India officially recognise, as of August 2021?
questions.questionHtml: How many classical dance forms does the Sangeet Natak Akademi in India officially recognise, as of August 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 8.

Key Points

  • Eight dance forms have been acknowledged by Sangeet Natak Akademi as classical dance forms of India as of August 2021.
    • The classical dance form originated from the Natya Shastra.
    • Classical dance has a deep-rooted relationship with the Natya Shastra where the specific features of each of the Classical dance forms have been mentioned.
    • There are 8 classical dance forms in India as per the source and scholars:
      • Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Kathakali, Sattriya, Manipuri and Mohiniyattam.
    • The Cultural Ministry of India has included Chhau in the list of classical dances make a total of 9 classical dance forms.
    • The 8 basic technicalities that are expressed in classical dance are given below:
      • Shringar: Love
      • Hasya: Humorous
      • Karuna: Sorrow
      • Raudra: Anger
      • Veer: Heroism
      • Bhayanak: Fear
      • Bibhats: Disgust
      • Adbhoot: Wonder

Additional Information

  • In India, dance forms can be broadly classified into 2 categories:
    • classical and folk dance form
  • These dance forms have been originated from different parts of India as per the local tradition.
  • Folk dance, on the other hand, emerged from the local tradition of the respective state, ethnic or geographic regions.
